children.text: śivaḥ śaktyā yukto yadi bhavati śaktaḥ prabhavituṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, only when united with <s>Śakti</s>, becomes capable of creating;

children.text: na ced evaṃ devo na khalu kuśalaḥ spanditum api
children.translated_text: otherwise, the God is indeed not able even to stir.
Therefore, You who are worshipped even by <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Virañci</s> and others—

children.text: praṇantuṃ stotuṃ vā katham akṛtapuṇyaḥ prabhavati
children.translated_text: how can one who has not acquired merit be capable of saluting or praising You?

children.text: śivaḥ śaktyā yukto yadi bhavati śaktaḥ prabhavituṃ
na ced evaṃ devo na khalu kuśalaḥ spanditum api
praṇantuṃ stotuṃ vā katham akṛtapuṇyaḥ prabhavati

children.translated_text: Gathering the finest dust born from the lotus of Your feet,
<s>Virañci</s> (Brahmā) fashions the worlds without deficiency;

children.text: vahaty enaṃ śauriḥ katham api sahasreṇa śirasāṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Śauri</s> (Viṣṇu) bears this [dust] somehow upon his thousand heads;
<s>Hara</s> (Śiva), pulverizing it, performs the rite of smearing himself with ashes.

children.text: vahaty enaṃ śauriḥ katham api sahasreṇa śirasāṃ

children.translated_text: For those steeped in ignorance, a sun-city dispelling the inner darkness;
for the dull-witted, a cascading stream of nectar from the cluster of consciousness;
for the destitute, a chain of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems; for those drowning in the ocean of birth,
You, O Goddess, are the tusk of <s>Murāri's</s> (Viṣṇu's) boar-form.
Other hosts of deities grant refuge and boons with their hands;
You alone do not display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.

children.text: bhayāt trātuṃ dātuṃ phalam api ca vāñchāsamadhikaṃ
children.translated_text: To protect from fear and to grant fruit exceeding desire—

children.text: śaraṇye lokānāṃ tava hi caraṇāv eva nipuṇau
children.translated_text: O refuge of the worlds, Your two feet alone are skilled in these, indeed.

children.text: bhayāt trātuṃ dātuṃ phalam api ca vāñchāsamadhikaṃ
śaraṇye lokānāṃ tava hi caraṇāv eva nipuṇau

children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, having worshipped You, O Mother of good fortune for those who bow,

children.text: purā nārī bhūtvā puraripum api kṣobham anayat
children.translated_text: formerly became a woman and brought even the Destroyer of Cities (<s>Śiva</s>) to agitation.
<s>Smara</s> (Kāma) too, having bowed to You, with a body delectable to <s>Rati's</s> eyes,

children.text: munīnām apy antaḥ prabhavati hi mohāya mahatām
children.translated_text: prevails in deluding even the minds of great sages.

children.text: purā nārī bhūtvā puraripum api kṣobham anayat
munīnām apy antaḥ prabhavati hi mohāya mahatām
dhanuḥ pauṣpaṃ maurvī madhukaramayī pañca viśikhā
children.translated_text: His bow is of flowers, his bowstring of bees, his five arrows [of blossoms],
Spring is his general, the Malaya breeze his war-chariot—

children.text: tathāpy ekaḥ sarvaṃ himagirisute kām api kṛpāṃ
children.translated_text: yet alone he conquers all this [world], O Daughter of the Snow Mountain, having obtained

children.text: apāṅgāt te labdhvā jagad idam anaṅgo vijayate
children.translated_text: some inexplicable grace from Your sidelong glance— <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One) triumphs.

children.text: dhanuḥ pauṣpaṃ maurvī madhukaramayī pañca viśikhā
tathāpy ekaḥ sarvaṃ himagirisute kām api kṛpāṃ
apāṅgāt te labdhvā jagad idam anaṅgo vijayate

children.translated_text: With a tinkling girdle of gold, with breasts heavy as the frontal globes of a young elephant,
slender at the waist, with a face like the full autumn moon,

children.text: dhanur bāṇān pāśaṃ sṛṇim api dadhānā karatalaiḥ
children.translated_text: holding bow, arrows, noose, and goad in Her hands—
may the heroic splendor of the Destroyer of Cities (<s>Śiva</s>) [i.e., His consort <s>Tripurasundarī</s>] stand before us.

children.text: dhanur bāṇān pāśaṃ sṛṇim api dadhānā karatalaiḥ

children.translated_text: In the midst of the ocean of nectar, surrounded by groves of celestial trees,
on the Jewel Island, in a grove of <s>kadamba</s> trees, within a palace of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gems,
upon a couch in the form of <s>Śiva</s>, reclining on Supreme <s>Śiva</s> as Your seat—

children.text: bhajanti tvāṃ dhanyāḥ kati cana cidānandalaharīm
children.translated_text: the fortunate few worship You, the Wave of Consciousness-Bliss.

children.text: bhajanti tvāṃ dhanyāḥ kati cana cidānandalaharīm
mahīṃ mūlādhāre kam api maṇipūre hutavahaṃ
children.translated_text: Earth in the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, water in the <s>Maṇipūra</s>, fire

children.text: sthitaṃ svādhiṣṭhāne hṛdi marutam ākāśam upari
children.translated_text: established in <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>, wind in the heart, space above,

children.text: mano 'pi bhrūmadhye sakalam api bhittvā kulapathaṃ
children.translated_text: mind too between the brows—having pierced the entire <s>kulapatha</s> (path of the Kuṇḍalinī),

children.text: sahasrāre padme saha rahasi patyā viharasi
children.translated_text: You sport with Your Lord in secret in the thousand-petaled lotus.

children.text: mahīṃ mūlādhāre kam api maṇipūre hutavahaṃ
sthitaṃ svādhiṣṭhāne hṛdi marutam ākāśam upari
mano 'pi bhrūmadhye sakalam api bhittvā kulapathaṃ
sahasrāre padme saha rahasi patyā viharasi

children.translated_text: With streams of nectar-showers flowing from within Your two feet,
irrigating the universe, and again through the greatness of the <s>rasāmnāya</s>,
having reached Your own place, in a coil like a serpent,

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ kṛtvā svapiṣi kulakuṇḍe kuhariṇi
children.translated_text: making Yourself [into that form], You sleep in the hollow of the <s>kulakuṇḍa</s>.

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ kṛtvā svapiṣi kulakuṇḍe kuhariṇi

children.translated_text: By four <s>Śrīkaṇṭhas</s> and five <s>Śivayuvatīs</s> (young Śiva-consorts),
differentiated from <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, these nine being the root-natures (<s>mūlaprakṛti</s>),
forty-three [triangles], with circles of eight-petaled and sixteen-petaled [lotuses] in earth-divisions,
together with three lines, the corners of Your [Śrī] <s>cakra</s> are formed.
To measure Your beauty, O Daughter of the Snow Mountain,
the foremost poets, <s>Virañci</s> (Brahmā) and others, somehow attempt—
for beholding it, the celestial women, out of eagerness, mentally seek
that state of union with <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva) which is unattainable even by austerities.
A man who is aged, unpleasing to the eyes, dull in amorous arts—
upon whom Your sidelong glance falls, him [young women] pursue by the hundreds,
with loosened braids, with garments slipping from the pitchers of their breasts,
their girdles snapping by force, their silk garments falling away.
Fifty-six [rays] in earth, fifty-two in water,
sixty-two in fire, fifty-four in wind,

children.text: divi dviḥṣattriṃśan manasi ca catuḥṣaṣṭir iti ye
children.translated_text: seventy-two in heaven, and sixty-four in mind—these are the rays,

children.text: mayūkhās teṣām apy upari tava pādāmbujayugam
children.translated_text: yet above even these is the pair of Your lotus feet.

children.text: divi dviḥ-ṣat-triṃśan manasi ca catuḥ-ṣaṣṭir iti ye
mayūkhās teṣām apy upari tava pādāmbu-ja-yugam

children.translated_text: Radiant as autumnal moonlight, wearing the moon-adorned matted-hair crown,
holding in Her hands a crystal rosary bestowing boons and protection, and a book—

children.text: sakṛn na tvā natvā katham iva stāṃ saṃnidadhate
children.translated_text: having bowed to You but once, how can [the devotees] not possess
speeches sweet with the sweetness of honey, milk, and grapes?

children.text: sakṛn na tvā natvā katham iva stāṃ saṃnidadhate

children.translated_text: Those saintly ones who worship You, <s>Aruṇā</s> (the Dawn-hued One),

children.text: bhajante ye santaḥ kati cid aruṇām eva bhavatīm
children.translated_text: whose radiance is like the morning sun upon the lotus-forest of great poets' minds—
they compose, with waves of the freshest <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment),

children.text: gabhīrābhir vāgbhir vidadhati satāṃ rañjanam amī
children.translated_text: with profound words, delight for the virtuous—the beloved of <s>Virañci</s> (Brahmā, i.e., <s>Sarasvatī</s>).

children.text: bhajante ye santaḥ kati cid aruṇām eva bhavatīm

children.translated_text: With the <s>Sāvitrī</s> goddesses of speech, radiant as moonstone broken in lustre,

children.text: vaśinyādyābhis tvāṃ saha janani saṃcintayati yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vaśinī</s> and others—whoever contemplates You together with them, O Mother,

children.text: sa kartā kāvyānāṃ bhavati mahatāṃ bhaṅgisubhagair
children.translated_text: he becomes the creator of great poems, with graceful
words fragrant-sweet as the lotus-face of <s>Vāgdevī</s> (Sarasvatī).

children.text: vaśiny-ādyābhis tvāṃ saha janani saṃcintayati yaḥ
sa kartā kāvyānāṃ bhavati mahatāṃ bhaṅgi-su-bhagair

children.translated_text: One who meditates upon the entire heaven and earth as immersed in redness

children.text: divaṃ sarvām urvīm aruṇimanigmagnāṃ smarati yaḥ
children.translated_text: through the lustre-rays of Your body, like pathways of the freshest sun—
for him there come women with timid deer-like eyes,
including <s>Urvaśī</s> herself—how many celestial courtesans become subject to him!

children.text: divaṃ sarvām urvīm aruṇima-nigmagnāṃ smarati yaḥ
saha urvaśyā vaśyāḥ kati-kati na gīrvāṇa-gaṇikā
mukhaṃ binduṃ kṛtvā kucayugam adhas tasya tadadho
children.translated_text: Making the face the <s>bindu</s> (dot), the pair of breasts below it, below that

children.text: harārdhaṃ dhyāyed yo haramahiṣi te manmathakalām
children.translated_text: the half of <s>Hara</s>—whoever thus meditates upon Your <s>Manmatha</s>-<s>kalā</s> (erotic form), O Consort of <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: sa sadyaḥ saṃkṣobhaṃ nayati vanitā ity atilaghu
children.translated_text: he immediately brings women to agitation—and this is but a trifle—
he quickly sets the three worlds spinning, [appearing] with the sun and moon as the pair of breasts.

children.text: mukhaṃ binduṃ kṛtvā kuca-yugam adhas tasya tad-adho
ha-rārdhaṃ dhyāyed yo hara-mahiṣi te manmatha-kalām
sa sadyaḥ saṃkṣobhaṃ nayati vanitā ity ati-laghu

children.translated_text: One who holds You in his heart, radiating ambrosia from [Your] limbs

children.text: hṛdi tvām ādhatte himakaraśilāmūrtim iva yaḥ
children.translated_text: in clusters of rays, as if an image fashioned from moonstone—

children.text: sa sarpāṇāṃ darpaṃ śamayati śakuntādhipa iva
children.translated_text: he allays the pride of serpents like <s>Garuḍa</s> (king of birds),
and with his gaze, [flowing] like a stream of nectar, he soothes those afflicted by fever.

children.text: hṛdi tvām ādhatte hima-kara-śilā-mūrtim iva yaḥ
sa sarpāṇāṃ darpaṃ śamayati śakuntādhipa iva

children.translated_text: Thin as a streak of lightning, consisting of the sun, moon, and fire,

children.text: niṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇām apy upari kamalānāṃ tava kalām
children.translated_text: Your <s>kalā</s> (subtle form) seated above the six lotuses—
great souls, beholding it in the great lotus-forest [of the <s>sahasrāra</s>], with minds
freed from the impurity of <s>māyā</s>, experience a supreme wave of bliss.

children.text: niṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇām apy upari kamalānāṃ tava kalām
bhavāni tvaṃ dāse mayi vitara dṛṣṭiṃ sakaruṇāṃ
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhavānī</s>, bestow upon me, Your servant, a compassionate glance'—

children.text: iti stotuṃ vāñchan kathayati bhavāni tvam iti yaḥ
children.translated_text: one who, wishing thus to praise You, merely utters 'O <s>Bhavānī</s>, You—'
at that very moment You grant him the state of union with You,
whose feet are worshipped with shining crowns by <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: bhavāni tvaṃ dāse mayi vitara dṛṣṭiṃ sa-karuṇāṃ
iti stotuṃ vāñchan kathayati bhavāni tvam iti yaḥ
tada aiva tvaṃ tasmai diśasi nija-sāyujya-padavīṃ
tvayā hṛtvā vāmaṃ vapur aparitṛptena manasā
children.translated_text: Having taken the left half of [<s>Śaṃbhu's</s>] body, with a mind still unsatisfied,

children.text: śarīrārdhaṃ śaṃbhor aparam api śaṅke hṛtam abhūt
children.translated_text: I suspect You seized the other half of <s>Śaṃbhu's</s> body as well—

children.text: tathā hi tvadrūpaṃ sakalam aruṇābhaṃ trinayanaṃ
children.translated_text: for thus Your form is entirely reddish, three-eyed,
bent forward with breasts, wearing a crown with the crescent moon.

children.text: tvayā hṛtvā vāmaṃ vapur a-paritṛptena manasā
śarīrārdhaṃ śaṃbhor aparam api śaṅke hṛtam abhūt
tathā hi tvad-rūpaṃ sa-kalam aruṇa-ābhaṃ tri-nayanaṃ
jagat sūte dhātā harir avati rudraḥ kṣapayate
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Brahmā) creates the world, <s>Hari</s> preserves it, <s>Rudra</s> destroys it,

children.text: tiras kurvann etat svam api vapur īśas tirayati
children.translated_text: <s>Īśa</s>, causing this [world] to vanish, himself also disappears,

children.text: sadāpūrvaḥ sarvaṃ tad idam anugṛhṇāti ca śivas
children.translated_text: <s>Sadāśiva</s>, ever-new, blesses all this—
all in obedience to Your command, by the momentary movement of Your eyebrow-creepers.

children.text: jagat sūte dhātā harir avati rudraḥ kṣapayate
tiras kurvann etat svam api vapur īśas tirayati
sadā-pūrvaḥ sarvaṃ tad idam anugṛhṇāti ca śivas

children.translated_text: Of the three gods born of the three <s>guṇas</s>, O Auspicious One,

children.text: bhavet pūjā pūjā tava caraṇayor yā viracitā
children.translated_text: the worship offered to Your feet becomes their worship [as well].
For near the gem-studded pedestal that bears Your feet,
these [gods] stand perpetually with folded hands raised to their crowns.

children.text: bhavet pūjā pūjā tava caraṇayor yā viracitā
virañciḥ pañcatvaṃ vrajati harir āpnoti viratiṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Virañci</s> (Brahmā) meets destruction, <s>Hari</s> reaches cessation,

children.text: vināśaṃ kīnāśo bhajati dhanado yāti nidhanam
children.translated_text: <s>Kīnāśa</s> (Yama) undergoes ruin, <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) goes to his end,
the host of <s>Mahendra</s> (Indra) too [perishes] with closed eyes—
in this great dissolution, Your Lord (<s>Śiva</s>) alone sports, O <s>Satī</s>.

children.text: virañciḥ pañcatvaṃ vrajati harir āpnoti viratiṃ
vināśaṃ kīnāśo bhajati dhana-do yāti nidhanam
japo jalpaḥ śilpaṃ sakalam api mudrāviracanā
children.translated_text: May my speech be <s>japa</s> (prayer), all my manual arts be <s>mudrā</s>-formation,
my walking be circumambulation, eating be the rite of oblation,
my lying down be prostration, all comfort be seen as self-offering—

children.text: saparyāparyāyas tava bhavatu yan me vilasitam
children.translated_text: may whatever I do become synonymous with Your worship.

children.text: japo jalpaḥ śilpaṃ sa-kalam api mudrā-viracanā
saparyā-paryāyas tava bhavatu yan me vilasitam

children.translated_text: Giving wealth to the needy ceaselessly, in accord with their desires,
lavishly scattering the nectar-fragrance of beauty—
may my life be immersed in Your foot, beautiful as a <s>mandāra</s> flower-cluster;
immersing, may I attain six-footedness [like a bee] with my sense-organs and limbs.
Even having tasted the nectar that wards off the dread of old age and death,
the celestials—<s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), <s>Śatamakha</s> (Indra), and others—perish.
That <s>Śaṃbhu</s> swallowed the terrible <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison [yet survived]—

children.text: na śaṃbhos tanmūlaṃ tava janani tāṭaṅkamahimā
children.translated_text: is that not due, O Mother, to the power of Your earrings [which rendered the poison harmless]?

children.text: na śaṃbhos tan-mūlaṃ tava janani tāṭaṅka-mahimā

children.translated_text: 'Avoid the crown of <s>Virañci</s> (Brahmā) [at Your feet]! You stumble on the hard tiara of the Slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (Viṣṇu)!
Dash aside the crown of the Enemy of <s>Jambha</s> (Indra)!'—
when these [gods] bow down and [<s>Śiva</s>] forcefully approaches [Your] chamber,
this speech of Your attendants [urging <s>Śiva</s> to rise] prevails gloriously.
Having encompassed the entire universe with sixty-four <s>tantras</s>,
each devoted to bestowing its particular <s>siddhi</s> (supernatural power), <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva) remained—
yet again, at Your insistence, accomplishing all human goals at once,

children.text: svatantraṃ te tantraṃ kṣititalam avātītarad idam
children.translated_text: Your independent <s>tantra</s> (the Śrīvidyā) descended upon this earth.

children.text: sva-tantraṃ te tantraṃ kṣiti-talam avātītarad idam
śivaḥ śaktiḥ kāmaḥ kṣitir atha raviḥ śītakiraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Kṣiti</s> (Earth), then <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Śītakiraṇa</s> (Moon),

children.text: smaro haṃsaḥ śakras tad anu ca parāmāraharayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), and thereafter <s>Para</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Hari</s>—
these syllables, joined at their ends with the three <s>hrīṃ</s> (<s>hṛllekhā</s>) syllables,

children.text: bhajante varṇās te tava janani nāmāvayavatām
children.translated_text: form the constituent parts of Your name, O Mother.

children.text: śivaḥ śaktiḥ kāmaḥ kṣitir atha raviḥ śīta-kiraṇaḥ
smaro haṃsaḥ śakras tad anu ca parā-māra-harayaḥ
bhajante varṇās te tava janani nāmāvayavatām
smaraṃ yoniṃ lakṣmīṃ tritayam idam ādau tava manor
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (ka), <s>Yoni</s> (e), <s>Lakṣmī</s> (ī)—placing this triad at the beginning of Your <s>mantra</s>,
some [adepts], O Eternal One, relishing boundless great enjoyment,
recite [the <s>mantra</s>] with a rosary strung of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gems,
offering hundreds of oblations of fragrant ghee into the fire of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: smaraṃ yoniṃ lakṣmīṃ tritayam idam ādau tava manor

children.translated_text: You are the body of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>; the moon and sun are the pair of breasts—
I consider Your self, O Blessed One, to be the immaculate self of <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva).
Therefore the relationship between You two stands as 'remainder and possessor-of-remainder'
by virtue of mutual identity, both being absorbed in supreme bliss.

children.text: tavā atmānaṃ manye bhagavati bhava-ātmānam an-agham
ataḥ śeṣaḥ śeṣi īty ayam ubhaya-sādhāraṇatayā
manas tvaṃ vyoma tvaṃ marud asi marutsārathir asi
children.translated_text: You are mind, You are space, You are wind, You are the charioteer of wind (fire),

children.text: tvam āpas tvaṃ bhūmis tvayi pariṇatāyāṃ na hi param
children.translated_text: You are water, You are earth—when You have transformed [into all], nothing remains beyond.
You transform Your own self into the form of the universe,
yet bear the form of Consciousness-Bliss, O Consort of <s>Śiva</s>, through Your essential nature.

children.text: manas tvaṃ vyoma tvaṃ marud asi marut-sārathir asi
tvam āpas tvaṃ bhūmis tvayi pariṇatāyāṃ na hi param

children.translated_text: Stationed in Your <s>Ājñā-cakra</s>, bearing the radiance of ten million suns and moons,
I worship that Supreme <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, embraced at His side by the Supreme Consciousness (<s>Paracit</s>),
worshipping whom with devotion, in a realm beyond [the light of] sun, moon, and fire,
the world dwells in the abode of [spiritual] light, though [physically] lightless.
In the <s>Viśuddhi</s> [cakra], pure, clear as crystal, the progenitor of space—
I worship <s>Śiva</s> and also the Goddess, equal to <s>Śiva</s> in Her pursuits,
by whose radiance, following the path of moonbeams,
the world, its inner darkness dispelled, shines forth like a <s>cakora</s> bird [delighting in moonlight].
Delighting solely in the nectar of the fully-blossoming lotus of pure awareness—

children.text: bhaje haṃsadvaṃdvaṃ kim api mahatāṃ mānasacaram
children.translated_text: I worship that ineffable pair of swans dwelling in the lake of the great souls,
from whose conversation the eighteen-fold <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) manifests,

children.text: yad ādatte doṣād guṇam akhilam adbhyaḥ paya iva
children.translated_text: who extract the good from the bad, as [swans separate] milk from water.

children.text: bhaje haṃsa-dvaṃdvaṃ kim api mahatāṃ mānasa-caram
yad ādatte doṣād guṇam a-khilam adbhyaḥ paya iva

children.translated_text: In Your <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>, presiding over the fire, ever-engaged—

children.text: tam īḍe saṃvartaṃ janani mahatīṃ tāṃ ca samayām
children.translated_text: I praise that <s>Saṃvarta</s> (dissolution-fire) and that great <s>Samayā</s> (the Goddess), O Mother,
at whose glance the worlds burn in the great fury of wrath—

children.text: dayārdrā dṛṣṭis te śiśiram upacāraṃ racayati
children.translated_text: [yet] Your compassion-moistened gaze provides a cooling remedy.

children.text: tam īḍe saṃvartaṃ janani mahatīṃ tāṃ ca samayām
dayā-ārdrā dṛṣṭis te śiśiram upacāraṃ racayati

children.translated_text: Accompanied by <s>Śakti</s> whose flashing dispels darkness—like lightning,
adorned as with <s>Indra's</s> bow (rainbow) by the glow of various sparkling jewel-ornaments,

children.text: tava śyāmaṃ meghaṃ kam api maṇipūraikaśaraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: I worship Your dark cloud [<s>Śiva</s>], indefinable, abiding solely in the <s>Maṇipūra</s>,
raining [bliss] upon the three worlds scorched by the sun of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: tava śyāmaṃ meghaṃ kam api maṇi-pūra-eka-śaraṇaṃ

children.translated_text: In Your base, the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, together with <s>Samayā</s> who delights in dance,
I worship the Nine-formed One, the dancer of the great <s>tāṇḍava</s> of the nine <s>rasas</s>.
Through both of these [Śiva and Śakti], indicating both modes [creation and dissolution], out of compassion,
endowed with [both] a lord, this world was born, having father and mother.

children.text: tavā adhāre mūle saha samayayā lāsya-parayā

children.translated_text: Your golden crown, densely set with celestial gems that have become rubies—

children.text: kirīṭaṃ te haimaṃ himagirisute kīrtayati yaḥ
children.translated_text: whoever celebrates it, O Daughter of the Snow Mountain,
would he not regard the crescent moon, dappled with the shade of a bird's nest,

children.text: dhanuḥ śaunāsīraṃ kim iti na nibadhnāti dhiṣaṇām
children.translated_text: as the rainbow-bow of <s>Indra</s>?

children.text: kirīṭaṃ te haimaṃ hima-giri-sute kīrtayati yaḥ
dhanuḥ śaunāsīraṃ kim iti na nibadhnāti dhiṣaṇām

children.translated_text: May Your mass of hair, O <s>Śivā</s>, dispel our darkness—
dense, smooth, dark as the destroyed indigo-lily grove—
whose natural fragrance, I believe, causes the flowers
from the garden-trees of the Slayer of <s>Bala</s> (Indra) to dwell therein, seeking to perceive it.
Bearing vermilion, with the deep darkness of the mass of heavy tresses
holding captive, as it were, the rays of the fresh sun with clusters of [dark] lustre—
may the parting-line of Your hair, like an overflow-channel
of the river of the beauty-wave of Your face, grant us welfare.
With naturally curling locks possessing the beauty of young bees,
Your face, surrounded [by them], mocks the beauty of the lotus.
In its gentle smile, beautiful with the filament-lustre of the teeth,
the bees that are <s>Smara's</s> (Kāma's, i.e., <s>Śiva</s> the destroyer of Kāma's) eyes become intoxicated by the fragrance.
Your forehead, spotlessly radiant with the lustre of beauty, shines—
I consider it a second fragment of the crescent moon of Your crown;

children.text: viparyāsanyāsād ubhayam api saṃbhūya ca mithaḥ
children.translated_text: through the transposition of their placement, both combining together,
the plaster of nectar transforms into the full moon.

children.text: viparyāsa-nyāsād ubhayam api saṃbhūya ca mithaḥ

children.translated_text: Your eyebrows, slightly arched, engaged in dispelling the fear of the world—
held as a bowstring by Your two eyes, [dark] like bees—
I consider them the bow of the Lord of Love (<s>Rati's</s> husband), held in left and right hands,

children.text: prakoṣṭhe muṣṭau ca sthagayati nigūḍhāntaram ume
children.translated_text: concealing the hidden [arrow] between forearm and fist, O <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: prakoṣṭhe muṣṭau ca sthagayati nigūḍhāntaram ume
ahaḥ sūte savyaṃ tava nayanam arkātmakatayā
children.translated_text: Your right eye, being of the nature of the Sun, creates the day;
Your left, being of the nature of the Moon (lord of night), produces the night.
Your third eye, with the lustre of a half-opened golden lotus,
produces the twilight that moves between day and night.

children.text: ahaḥ sūte savyaṃ tava nayanam arka-ātmakatayā

children.translated_text: Vast, auspicious, of manifest radiance, unconquerable by blue lotuses,
a receptacle of streams of compassion, somehow sweet, like [the city] <s>Bhogavatī</s> (of the <s>Nāgas</s>)—
Your gaze, O <s>Avantī</s>, victorious in the expanse of many cities,
is surely worthy of being called by each of those [city] names.
Your pair of ears, solely delighting in the nectar of the flower-clusters of poets' compositions,
the young bees that are Your sidelong glances—
seeing these two [ears] restless with eagerness to taste the new <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor),
slightly reddened by association with jealousy, [like] a false eye
Moist with erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) toward <s>Śiva</s>, contemptuous toward other faces,
wrathful toward <s>Gaṅgā</s>, filled with wonder at the exploits of the Lord of the Mountain,
afraid of <s>Hara</s>'s serpents, victorious over the beauty of the lotus,

children.text: sakhīṣu smerā te mayi janani dṛṣṭiḥ sakaruṇā
children.translated_text: smiling toward friends—your gaze, O Mother, is compassionate toward me.

children.text: sakhīṣu smerā te mayi janani dṛṣṭiḥ sa-karuṇā
gate karṇābhyarṇaṃ garuta iva pakṣmāṇi dadhatī
children.translated_text: Reaching close to the ears, bearing eyelashes like wings of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
accomplishing the dispelling of the tranquility-nectar in the mind of the destroyer of the cities,
these two eyes, O bud-like crown-jewel of the family of the lord of mountains,
display the playful sport of the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), drawn to the ear.

children.text: gate karṇābhyarṇaṃ garuta iva pakṣmāṇi dadhatī

children.translated_text: Displaying a division into three colors, mixed with dark collyrium,
this triad of your eyes shines forth, O beloved of <s>Īśāna</s>,
as if bearing the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)—<s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s>—

children.text: rajaḥ sattvaṃ bibhrat tama iti guṇānāṃ trayam iva
children.translated_text: in order to create anew the gods <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, who had ceased [their functions].

children.text: rajaḥ sattvaṃ bibhrat tama iti guṇānāṃ trayam iva

children.translated_text: O you whose heart is subject to <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of creatures), to purify us
with your compassionate eyes of red, white, and dark hues,

children.text: nadaḥ śoṇo gaṅgā tapanatanayeti dhruvam amuṃ
children.translated_text: you surely bring about the confluence of three sacred rivers—
the <s>Śoṇa</s> (Red River), the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the <s>Tapanatanayā</s> (Yamunā, daughter of the Sun), O sinless one.

children.text: nadaḥ śoṇo gaṅgā tapana-tanaya īti dhruvam amuṃ

children.translated_text: In [the lake of] your ear, frightened by the tale-bearing of the eyes to the ear,
the unblinking <s>śapharikā</s> (small fish) surely hide in the water;
and <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), like a blue lotus with petals shut as if with doors,

children.text: jahāti pratyūṣe niśi ca vighaṭayya praviśati
children.translated_text: departs at dawn and enters again at night, opening [the petals].

children.text: jahāti pratyūṣe niśi ca vighaṭayya praviśati

children.translated_text: The world undergoes dissolution and creation by the closing and opening of [your eyes]—
so say the sages, O daughter of the king of mountains;

children.text: tvadunmeṣāj jātaṃ jagad idam aśeṣaṃ pralayataḥ
children.translated_text: since this entire universe arose from the opening of your eyes, I think
your eyes have given up blinking in order to protect it from dissolution.

children.text: tvad-unmeṣāj jātaṃ jagad idam a-śeṣaṃ pralayataḥ

children.translated_text: With your long gaze, having the luster of a slightly opened blue lotus,

children.text: davīyāṃsaṃ dīnaṃ snapaya kṛpayā mām api śive
children.translated_text: bathe even me, who am distant and wretched, with your compassion, O <s>Śive</s> (auspicious one);

children.text: anenāyaṃ dhanyo bhavati na ca te hānir iyatā
children.translated_text: by this [act] one becomes blessed, and there is no loss to you thereby—

children.text: vane vā harmye vā samakaranipāto himakaraḥ
children.translated_text: the moon falls equally on the forest or the palace.

children.text: davīyāṃsaṃ dīnaṃ snapaya kṛpayā mām api śive
anena ayaṃ dhanyo bhavati na ca te hānir iyatā
vane vā harmye vā sama-kara-nipāto hima-karaḥ

children.translated_text: The curved pair of your brow-lines, O daughter of the king of mountains,
in whom does it not arouse the curiosity of the bow of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>)?
Where, crossing transversely beyond the path of the ear, the shining
sidelong glance imparts the skill of fitting the arrow to the bowstring.
With a pair of ear-ornaments reflected in the expanse of your radiant cheeks—

children.text: catuścakraṃ manye tava mukham idaṃ manmatharatham
children.translated_text: I consider this face of yours to be the four-wheeled chariot of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love),
mounting which, the great warrior <s>Māra</s> (Love) overpowers
the Lord of the <s>Pramathas</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), [whose chariot is] the earth with the sun and moon as wheels, who had [previously] been victorious.

children.text: catuś-cakraṃ manye tava mukham idaṃ manmatha-ratham

children.translated_text: As you drink ceaselessly, O consort of <s>Śarva</s>, through the cup-like ears,
the eloquent verses of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, waves of the river of nectar,
your cluster of earrings, with head nodding in appreciative praise,

children.text: jhaṇatkārais tāraiḥ prativacanam ācaṣṭae iva te
children.translated_text: seems to speak a reply with their clear jingling sounds.

children.text: jhaṇat-kārais tāraiḥ prativacanam ācaṣṭae iva te

children.translated_text: This bamboo-stem of your nose, O banner of the lineage of the Snowy Mountain,

children.text: tvadīyo nedīyaḥ phalatu phalam asmākam ucitam
children.translated_text: being so near [to your face], may it bear appropriate fruit for us;
bearing within it pearls formed by cool exhalations,

children.text: samṛddhyā yas tāsāṃ bahir api ca muktāmaṇidharaḥ
children.translated_text: and by their abundance, bearing a pearl-gem [ornament] even on the outside.

children.text: tvadīyo nedīyaḥ phalatu phalam asmākam ucitam
samṛddhyā yas tāsāṃ bahir api ca muktā-maṇi-dharaḥ

children.translated_text: Of your lips, which are naturally red, O beautiful-toothed one, of the luster of the covering of your teeth,
I shall describe a likeness—may the coral vine produce [such] fruit!
The <s>bimba</s> fruit, reddened only by the reflection of that [lip],

children.text: tulām adhyāroḍhuṃ katham iva vilajjeta kalayā
children.translated_text: how could it, even by a fraction, shamelessly claim to ascend to equality?

children.text: tulām adhyāroḍhuṃ katham iva vilajjeta kalayā

children.translated_text: For the <s>cakora</s> birds drinking the network of moonlight from the smile of your moon-like face,
there was numbness of the beak due to excessive relish;
therefore, having a taste for the sour, they freely drink
the nectar-stream of the cool-rayed [moon] every night, thinking it to be <s>kāñcika</s> (sour gruel).
Unceasingly engaged in the repetitive recitation of the enumeration of the Lord's virtues,

children.text: japāpuṣpacchāyā tava janani jihvā jayati sā
children.translated_text: your tongue, O Mother, prevails, having the hue of the <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower;
seated at whose tip, the form of <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
[normally] transparent like crystal, transforms into a ruby-bodied one.

children.text: japā-puṣpa-cchāyā tava janani jihvā jayati sā

children.translated_text: Having conquered the <s>Daityas</s> (demons) in battle, by the armored [gods] whose helmets had been removed,
returning, averse to the leftover offerings of the destroyer of the three cities (<s>Śiva</s>) who is fierce-rayed,
by <s>Viśākha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), [your] morsels of betel, white as moonlight with pieces of camphor,
are eagerly dissolved, O Mother, from your mouth.
As <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) sings on the <s>vīṇā</s> the various heroic deeds of <s>Paśupati</s>,
when you begin to speak words of appreciation with nodding head,
by your sweetness [of voice], silencing the melody of the <s>vīṇā</s> strings,

children.text: nijāṃ vīṇāṃ vāṇī niculayati colena nibhṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṇī</s> quietly covers her own <s>vīṇā</s> with its cloth.

children.text: nijāṃ vīṇāṃ vāṇī niculayati colena nibhṛtam

children.translated_text: Clearly [held] at the fingertips by the Snowy Mountain [<s>Himālaya</s>] with paternal affection,
raised up by the Lord of the Mountain (<s>Śiva</s>) repeatedly in his eagerness to drink [from] your lips,
graspable by the hand of <s>Śambhu</s>, [like] the handle of a face-mirror, O daughter of the mountain—
how shall we describe your chin, which is beyond comparison?
Your neck, bristling always from the embrace of the arms of the destroyer of cities (<s>Śiva</s>),
bears the beauty of a lotus-stalk [supporting] the face-lotus;
naturally white, darkened by the thick paste of black <s>agaru</s> (aloe),
the necklace hanging below it bears the loveliness of a lotus fiber.
The three lines on your throat, O one skilled solely in the <s>gati</s>, <s>gamaka</s>, and <s>gīta</s> of music,
representing the count of the three strands (<s>guṇas</s>) tied at the marriage [ceremony],
shine like the boundary lines that determine the fixed arrangement
of the three <s>grāmas</s> (musical scales), which are the sources of various sweet <s>rāgas</s> (melodies).
The beauty of your four arm-creepers, soft as lotus stalks,
<s>Brahmā</s> (the lotus-born) praises with [his] four faces;
trembling from fear of the nails [of <s>Śiva</s>] since the first churning of <s>Andhaka</s> (the demon),
with the intention of offering simultaneously the gesture of fearlessness to [his] four heads.
Of your hands whose nails' radiance laughs at the color of fresh lotuses—

children.text: karāṇāṃ te kāntiṃ kathaya kathayāmaḥ katham ume
children.translated_text: how shall we describe their beauty, O <s>Umā</s>?

children.text: kayā cid vā sāmyaṃ bhajatu kalayā hanta kamalaṃ
children.translated_text: Perhaps the lotus may bear some comparison by a small fraction,
if it has petals reddened by the lac-dye from the soles of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s feet as she plays [upon it].

children.text: karāṇāṃ te kāntiṃ kathaya kathayāmaḥ katham ume
kayā cid vā sāmyaṃ bhajatu kalayā hanta kamalaṃ

children.translated_text: O Goddess, may this pair of breasts, equally suckled by <s>Skanda</s> and the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>),

children.text: tavedaṃ naḥ khedaṃ haratu satataṃ prasnutamukham
children.translated_text: with ever-flowing faces [of milk], remove our sorrow always;
seeing which, with heart agitated by doubt and causing laughter,
<s>Heramba</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) hastily feels his own two frontal globes with his trunk.

children.text: tava idaṃ naḥ khedaṃ haratu satataṃ prasnuta-mukham

children.translated_text: These two breasts of yours, like vessels of nectar and ruby,
let there be no doubt or trembling in our minds, O banner of the Mountain Lord;
for, having suckled from them, [yet] unknowing of the pleasure of union with a bride,
the two princes—the elephant-faced (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) and the piercer of <s>Krauñca</s> (<s>Skanda</s>)—remain [as youths] even today.
O Mother, your bosom bears a necklace of pure pearls
begun [to be strung] with pearls resembling the frontal globes of the young elephant of pride,
variegated within by the luster of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit-like lower lip,
as if it were the fame of the conqueror of the cities (<s>Śiva</s>), mixed with glory.
I think your breast-milk, O daughter of the Mountain, from the heart
overflows like the ocean of milk [through] the stream of <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence);

children.text: dayāvatyā dattaṃ draviḍaśiśur āsvādya tava yat
children.translated_text: for having tasted that [milk], given by you in compassion,
the <s>Draviḍa</s> child (<s>Jñānasambandhar</s>) became a lovely poet among mature poets.

children.text: dayāvatyā dattaṃ draviḍa-śiśur āsvādya tava yat

children.translated_text: In the deep lake of your navel, <s>Manasija</s> (the Mind-born, <s>Kāma</s>), his body
licked by the flames of <s>Hara</s>'s anger, took refuge;
from there arose a tendril of smoke, O daughter of the mountain—

children.text: janas tāṃ jānīte janani tava romāvalir iti
children.translated_text: people know that, O Mother, as the line of hair [on your belly].

children.text: janas tāṃ jānīte janani tava romāvalir iti

children.translated_text: That which, O <s>Śive</s>, resembles the slender, delicate waves of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),

children.text: kṛśe madhye kiṃ cij janani tava tad bhāti sudhiyām
children.translated_text: your slender waist, O Mother, appears to the wise
as the space between the two pitcher-like breasts, pressed against each other,
becoming thin [like the sky] and entering the cave of the navel.

children.text: kṛśe madhye kiṃ cij janani tava tad bhāti su-dhiyām

children.translated_text: A steady whirlpool of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with the creeper of the hair-line as the bud-like breast,
a basin for the fire of the splendor of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: rater līlāgāraṃ kim api tava nābhīti girije
children.translated_text: the pleasure-house of <s>Rati</s> (Love's consort)—your navel, O daughter of the mountain, is something indescribable;
a gateway to <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) for the eyes of the Lord of the Mountain (<s>Śiva</s>), it triumphs!

children.text: rater līlā-agāraṃ kim api tava nābhi īti giri-je

children.translated_text: Of [the waist] which is naturally slender, burdened by the weight of the breast-region, fatigued,

children.text: namanmūrter nābhau baliṣu śanakais truṭyatae iva
children.translated_text: bending in form, [appearing] at the navel and in the folds as if slowly breaking—
may there be well-being for the long-lasting stability of your waist,
[which is like] a young tree on the bank of a river whose bank has broken away, O daughter of the mountain.

children.text: naman-mūrter nābhau baliṣu śanakais truṭyatae iva

children.translated_text: Your breasts, bursting through the bodice fitted tightly to the freshly perspiring slopes,
rubbing against the root of the arms, [appearing] like golden pitchers—

children.text: tava trātuṃ bhaṅgād alam iti vilagnaṃ tanubhuvā
children.translated_text: [<s>Kāma</s>] the bodiless one, having clung [to your waist] as if to protect it from breaking,

children.text: tridhā naddhaṃ devi trivali lavalīvallibhir iva
children.translated_text: has tied it thrice, O Goddess, with the three folds [of skin] like <s>lavalī</s> creepers.

children.text: tava trātuṃ bhaṅgād alam iti vilagnaṃ tanu-bhuvā
tridhā naddhaṃ devi tri-vali lavalī-vallibhir iva

children.translated_text: The lord of the mountains, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, having taken from his own [mass]
weight and breadth, placed them upon your hips as if by theft;

children.text: atas te vistīrṇo gurur ayam aśeṣāṃ vasumatīṃ
children.translated_text: therefore, this broad and heavy forward-leaning mass of your hips
covers the entire earth and renders it lightweight.

children.text: atas te vistīrṇo gurur ayam a-śeṣāṃ vasumatīṃ

children.translated_text: Surpassing on both sides, with both thighs, the trunks of lordly elephants

children.text: ubhābhyām ūrubhyām ubhayam api nirjitya bhavatī
children.translated_text: and the clusters of stems of golden plantain trees,
with [your] well-rounded [knees], hardened by prostration to the Lord, O daughter of the mountain,
you have conquered even the pair of frontal globes of the divine elephant with your knees.

children.text: ubhābhyām ūrubhyām ubhayam api nirjitya bhavatī

children.translated_text: To defeat <s>Rudra</s>, O daughter of the mountain, your calves,

children.text: niṣaṅgau jaṅghe te viṣamaviśikho bāḍham akṛta
children.translated_text: [serving as] two quivers bearing doubled arrows, were surely made by the odd-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>);
at whose tips are seen the ten arrow-points [in the form of] the pair of feet,
disguised as toenails, sharpened solely on the whetstone of the crowns of the gods.

children.text: niṣaṅgau jaṅghe te vi-ṣama-viśikho bāḍham akṛta
śrutīnāṃ mūrdhāno dadhati tava yau śekharatayā
children.translated_text: Your two [feet], which the crowns of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas/Upaniṣads) bear as their crest-jewels—

children.text: mamāpy etau mātaḥ śirasi dayayā dhehi caraṇau
children.translated_text: O Mother, place those two feet upon my head as well, out of compassion;
whose washing-water is the river in the matted locks of <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>),
whose lac-ornament has the luster of the red crest-jewel of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).

children.text: śrutīnāṃ mūrdhāno dadhati tava yau śekharatayā
mama apy etau mātaḥ śirasi dayayā dhehi caraṇau

children.translated_text: We offer words of salutation to your pair of feet, delightful to the eyes,
radiant with clearly gleaming lac-dye;
with which the Lord of creatures (<s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Śiva</s>) is exceedingly jealous, desiring to strike
the <s>Kaṅkeli</s> (Aśoka) tree in the pleasure garden [which your feet kicked to make it bloom].
Having deliberately made a slip of the [family] name, and then bowing with embarrassment,
your Lord strikes [his own] forehead at [your] lotus-feet;
by <s>Śiva</s>'s enemy [<s>Kāma</s>], who has long since uprooted the thorn [of anger] created by fire [<s>Śiva</s>'s third eye],
[this is] celebrated with tinkling sounds like the striking of a balance [i.e., the anklets' music].
Skilled in traversing the snow-laden slopes of the Snowy Mountain, able to destroy snow,

children.text: niśāyāṃ nidrāṇāṃ niśi ca parabhāge ca viśadau
children.translated_text: luminous at night when [all] are asleep, and also in the latter part of the night,
being the supreme receptacle of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, surpassing the beauty of the <s>samayins</s> (devotees)—

children.text: sarojaṃ tvatpādau janani jayataś citram iha kim
children.translated_text: your feet, O Mother, triumph over the lotus; what wonder is there in this?

children.text: niśāyāṃ nidrāṇāṃ niśi ca para-bhāge ca viśadau
saro-jaṃ tvat-pādau janani jayataś citram iha kim
padaṃ te kāntīnāṃ prapadam apadaṃ devi vipadāṃ
children.translated_text: Your forefoot is the abode of beauty and the refuge from misfortune, O Goddess;
how has it been compared by the wise to the hard shell of a tortoise?
How indeed [was it that] at the time of the marriage ceremony, the destroyer of the cities (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: yad ādāya nyastaṃ dṛṣadi dayamānena manasā
children.translated_text: with compassionate mind, having taken [your foot], placed it upon a grinding stone?

children.text: padaṃ te kāntīnāṃ pra-padam a-padaṃ devi vipadāṃ
yad ādāya nyastaṃ dṛṣadi dayamānena manasā

children.translated_text: With toenails [shining like] moons that cause the lotus-hands of celestial women to close,

children.text: tarūṇāṃ divyānāṃ hasata iva te caṇḍi caraṇau
children.translated_text: your feet, O <s>Caṇḍī</s>, seem to laugh at the divine <s>kalpa</s> trees,
which give fruits to the prosperous with their sprout-like hand-tips,

children.text: daridrebhyo bhadrāṃ śriyam aniśam ahnāya dadatau
children.translated_text: [while your feet] give auspicious wealth to the poor ceaselessly, day after day.

children.text: tarūṇāṃ divyānāṃ hasata iva te caṇḍi caraṇau
daridrebhyo bhadrāṃ śriyam a-niśam ahnāya dadatau

children.translated_text: When, O Mother, tell me—may I, a seeker of knowledge,
drink the water that has washed your feet, tinged with lac-dye,
which, having the power to make even the naturally mute into poets,
imparts the flavor of the betel in the lotus-mouth of <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>)?
As if having begun to learn the playful game of your gait,

children.text: carantas te khelaṃ bhavanakalahaṃsā na jahati
children.translated_text: the royal swans of your palace do not abandon their sporting;
your lotus-foot, with the beautiful sound of gem-studded anklets,
seems to be teaching them [the art] of graceful flinging [of steps], O one of beautiful conduct.

children.text: carantas te khelaṃ bhavana-kala-haṃsā na jahati

children.translated_text: Curled in the hair, naturally straight in the gentle smile,

children.text: śirīṣābhā citte dṛṣad iva kaṭhorā kucataṭe
children.translated_text: delicate as <s>śirīṣa</s> (acacia) flowers in the heart, hard as stone on the breast-mounds,
exceedingly slender at the waist, broad in the region of the rising breasts—

children.text: jagat trātuṃ śaṃbhor jayati karuṇā kā cid aruṇā
children.translated_text: a certain reddish compassion of <s>Śambhu</s> triumphs, [existing] to protect the world!

children.text: śirīṣa-ābhā citte dṛṣad iva kaṭhorā kuca-taṭe
jagat trātuṃ śaṃbhor jayati karuṇā kā cid aruṇā

children.translated_text: You are the inner chamber of the enemy of the cities (<s>Śiva</s>); therefore the proper worship of your feet
is unattainable for those of wavering senses;

children.text: tathā hy ete nītāḥ śatamakhamukhāḥ siddhim atulāṃ
children.translated_text: for these [gods], led by <s>Indra</s> (the hundred-sacrificer) and others, have attained incomparable <s>siddhi</s> (perfection)
through the [powers of] <s>Aṇimā</s> and others, stationed at the doorstep of your [abode], [acting as] immortals.

children.text: tathā hy ete nītāḥ śata-makha-mukhāḥ siddhim a-tulāṃ

children.translated_text: Those who serve as your couch—<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s>—
<s>Śiva</s>, with a canopy fabricated from the reflection of his own pure radiance,
having attained redness from the reflection of your splendors,

children.text: śarīrī śṛṅgāro rasa iva dṛśāṃ dogdhi kutukam
children.translated_text: milks forth wonder for the eyes, as if the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) had taken bodily form.

children.text: śarīrī śṛṅgāro rasa iva dṛśāṃ dogdhi kutukam

children.translated_text: The stain is musk, the disc of the night-maker (moon) is made of water,
its digits are [made of] camphor packed in an emerald casket;
therefore, emptied daily by your enjoyment, this hollow [of the moon]

children.text: vidhir bhūyobhūyo nibiḍayati nūnaṃ tava kṛte
children.translated_text: is surely filled again and again by <s>Vidhī</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) for your sake.

children.text: vidhir bhūyo-bhūyo nibiḍayati nūnaṃ tava kṛte

children.translated_text: One who always meditates, 'I worship you, the eternal one, who are attended

children.text: niṣevye nitye tvām aham iti sadā bhāvayati yaḥ
children.translated_text: all around by the rays (<s>aṇimā</s> and other powers) born from your own body'—
is it any wonder that for him, who regards even the wealth of the three-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>) as a blade of grass,
the great fire of universal dissolution performs the <s>nīrājana</s> (waving of lights) ceremony?

children.text: niṣevye nitye tvām aham iti sadā bhāvayati yaḥ
kalatraṃ vaidhātraṃ katikati bhajante na kavayaḥ
children.translated_text: How many poets do not court the wife of <s>Vidhī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>)?

children.text: śriyo devyāḥ ko vā na bhavati patiḥ kair api dhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: And who does not become the lord of <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of wealth) with some riches?

children.text: mahādevaṃ hitvā tava sati satīnām acarame
children.translated_text: But except for <s>Mahādeva</s>, O <s>Satī</s>, O last (foremost) among chaste women,
even the <s>kuravaka</s> (Barleria) tree cannot easily attain the embrace of your breasts.

children.text: kalatraṃ vaidhātraṃ kati-kati bhajante na kavayaḥ
śriyo devyāḥ ko vā na bhavati patiḥ kair api dhanaiḥ
mahā-devaṃ hitvā tava sati satīnām a-carame

children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Āgamas</s> (scriptures) call her the Goddess of Speech, the wife of <s>Brahmā</s>;
the consort of <s>Hari</s> is <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); the companion of <s>Hara</s> is the daughter of the mountain;
but you are some fourth [power], of limitless and incomprehensible majesty;
O <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (Great Illusion), you delude the universe, O consort of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
He who worships you sports as the co-husband with <s>Vidhī</s> and <s>Hari</s> of <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
loosens the fidelity of <s>Rati</s> (Love's wife) with [his] beautiful form;
living long, having cut the bonds of <s>Paśupati</s> (worldly fetters),
he relishes the bliss called Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
Waving the lamp before the sun with lamp-flames,
offering <s>arghya</s> (water-offering) to the nectar-producing moon with drops of water from moonstone,
satisfying the ocean with its own waters—

children.text: tvadīyābhir vāgbhis tava janani vācāṃ stutir iyam
children.translated_text: such is this praise of the Goddess of Speech with your own words, O Mother.

children.text: tvadīyābhir vāgbhis tava janani vācāṃ stutir iyam

children.translated_text: Brought to the state of a jewel for the crown at [your] feet, the sun-gem,
with its rays held still within out of fear, smooth [and subdued]
He holds your face, reflected ceaselessly blooming,
fearlessly, like the moon in the lotus of his own heart.
With a chest bearing the weight of full, risen breasts, with a charming smile,
with sidelong glances, <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), with a body radiant like a blossoming <s>kadamba</s> tree,

children.text: harasya tvadbhrāntiṃ manasi janayām āsa madano
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> (Cupid) created in the mind of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) the delusion of you;

children.text: bhavatyā ye bhaktāḥ pariṇatir amīṣām iyam ume
children.translated_text: those who are your devotees, O <s>Umā</s>, this is the transformation that befalls them.

children.text: harasya tvad-bhrāntiṃ manasi janayām āsa madano
bhavatyā ye bhaktāḥ pariṇatir amīṣām iyam ume

children.translated_text: O treasure of eternal smiles, O one of limitless virtues, O one skilled in wisdom,
O one of unobstructed knowledge, O one whose sole abode is the mind devoted to self-discipline,
O one liberated by destiny, O one praised at the end of all <s>Nigamas</s> (Vedas),

children.text: nirātaṅke nitye nigamaya mamāpi stutim imām
children.translated_text: O fearless one, O eternal one, accept this hymn of mine as well.

children.text: nir-ātaṅke nitye nigamaya mama api stutim imām
